facts.material: plastic housing with electronics and loudspeaker (assumed)
facts.function: plays back pre-stored predator/animal call sounds to attract game

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 8519 covers sound recording or reproducing apparatus; the device reproduces stored sounds

Chapter 92 (heading 9208 decoy calls) covers mouth-blown/mechanical calls, and heading 9507 hunting requisites does not name electronic sound apparatus; the electrical sound-reproducing function is specifically described in 8519 (GRI 3(a) specificity)
GRI 6: 8519.81 using semiconductor media (stored digital sounds, assumed); sound reproducing only; not a cassette player; 8519.81.30 other; suffix .20 other (not an optical disc player)

rejected_alternatives.reason: applies to apparatus that also records; this device only reproduces pre-loaded calls (N334310's device recorded, hence .41)
decoy calls of heading 9208 are non-electrical (mouth-blown) instruments; the device is an electrical sound reproducer
hunting requisites heading yields to the more specific description of the electronic sound reproducing apparatus in 8519
a loudspeaker alone would not store or reproduce sounds

missing_facts: Does the unit also record sounds (then 8519.81.41.50)?
Are the calls stored on semiconductor memory (assumed) rather than cassette tape?
classification.rationale: A battery-operated device that plays back stored predator calls is a sound reproducing apparatus of heading 8519; the electrical playback function is more specifically described there than as a decoy call of 9208 or a hunting requisite of 9507. With sounds on semiconductor media and no recording capability, it falls in 'sound reproducing only: other', 8519.81.30.20. NY N334310 (in force) shows CBP placing a small battery-operated sound device in 8519.81, at .41.50 because that device also recorded.
